name: Battle of Courtrai
summary: At the Battle of Courtrai (Kortrijk, July 11, 1302), known as the 'Battle of the Golden Spurs' from the 500 golden spurs collected from dead French knights, a Flemish infantry militia of weavers and craftsmen defeats a French army under Robert of Artois. The Flemish Goedendag (a spiked club-staff hybrid) and the canal-and-ditch terrain nullify French cavalry charges; Robert of Artois and 1,000 knights are killed. Courtrai is one of the pivotal battles of medieval warfare: a well-trained, motivated infantry force defeats the flower of French chivalry on a prepared field.

_quarry.structural_significance: Second major demonstration (after Legnano, 1176) that infantry can defeat feudal cavalry; influences Swiss and Flemish military development; temporarily secures Flemish independence; the golden spurs become the symbol of Flemish national pride
